problems: The caption's payoff, 'the cord comes taut and pulls its clip off the first pot', never happens on screen: the whole last part (storyboard row 4 and the last 3 s of the film) is the same still view of the pots, with the cord lying in the rut and still running into the first pot. Nothing comes taut, nothing comes off, nothing moves.

The 'copper cord paying out behind it' doesn't look like a cord paying out. In rows 1-3 and the 25%/50% frames it's a straight, rigid, pale grey rod lying in the plank groove from the left edge of the frame to the cart. It doesn't sag or curve, it isn't copper-coloured, and you can't see it leave a drum or spool on the cart.

The two halves of the film don't connect. The cart part is a high side view of a cart on planks, then it cuts to a low view of pots by a palm trunk. You never see the cart and the pots in the same shot, so someone watching can't tell that the cart pulls on anything at the pots.
Is the drum motor driving anything? The small gear next to it hardly reads as turning, and in the storyboard the cart slides along at a steady speed. Nothing shows that the motor makes the cart move.

Framing: from storyboard frame 10 on, a pink flower blob creeps in at the bottom right and covers the corner. The cart sits in heavy shadow, so the deck and motor are dark brown on dark brown. A palm trunk takes up the left quarter of every pot frame.
posts.critique: This is a cart driving along a plank road, with a grey rod beside it, and then a still life of pots where the promised tug never happens. The caption tells a cause and effect that the film doesn't show at any point.
